mindFoundations.summary: Understanding perception, attention, memory, and interpretation.

keyIdeas: The brain filters far more information than it processes.
Memory is reconstructive, not a recording.

keyIdeas: Fight-or-flight is adaptive but costly when chronic.
Perceived threat matters more than actual threat.

mindFoundations.summary: Why humans make predictable thinking mistakes.
mindFoundations.title: Cognitive Bias and Decision Errors

howTheyThink: Pattern recognition across behavior and cognition.

psychologyCareers.focus: Whole-body health with awareness of mental factors.
psychologyCareers.title: Medical Doctor (Non-Psychiatric)

clinicalThinking.summary: Clinicians use both fast intuition and slow analysis.
clinicalThinking.title: Pattern Recognition vs Analytical Thinking
keyIdeas: Experienced clinicians recognize familiar patterns quickly.
Analytical thinking is used when patterns are unclear.

clinicalThinking.summary: Considering multiple possible explanations at once.
clinicalThinking.title: Differential Thinking
keyIdeas: Clinicians rank possibilities, not pick one early.

clinicalThinking.summary: Medicine operates under uncertainty, not certainty.
clinicalThinking.title: Probability and Uncertainty
whyItMatters: Clarifies why tests are not definitive.

clinicalThinking.title: Common Things Are Common
keyIdeas: Rare conditions are considered when evidence supports them.

clinicalThinking.summary: Clinicians actively counter known thinking errors.
clinicalThinking.title: Safeguards Against Cognitive Bias
whyItMatters: Medicine designs systems to reduce error.

cognitiveBiases.summary: The tendency to favor information that confirms existing beliefs.
cognitiveBiases.name: Confirmation Bias

cognitiveBiases.summary: Judging likelihood based on how easily examples come to mind.
realWorldExamples: Overestimating rare dangers after news coverage.
cognitiveBiases.name: Availability Heuristic
whyItMatters: Underestimates common but less vivid ones.
whyItHappens: Recent or vivid events feel more important.

cognitiveBiases.summary: Relying too heavily on the first piece of information encountered.
cognitiveBiases.name: Anchoring Bias
whyItMatters: Makes updates slower and less accurate.
whyItHappens: Adjustments from the anchor are insufficient.

cognitiveBiases.summary: Attributing others’ behavior to character rather than situation.
cognitiveBiases.name: Fundamental Attribution Error

whyTheMythExists: Mental health terms are used casually.
mentalHealthMyths.reality: Anxiety is a normal human response; disorders are defined by duration, intensity, and impact.
mentalHealthMyths.myth: Feeling anxious means you have an anxiety disorder.

whyTheMythExists: Mind and body are often discussed separately.
mentalHealthMyths.reality: Mental health reflects interactions between brain, body, environment, and experience.
mentalHealthMyths.myth: Mental health conditions are purely psychological.

mentalHealthMyths.reality: Psychological stress affects all humans regardless of strength or resilience.
Thoughtful discussion often improves insight and coping.
mentalHealthMyths.myth: Talking about mental health makes problems worse.

mentalHealthMyths.reality: Clinicians look for patterns over time, not isolated signs.

ethicsAndBoundaries.summary: Learning about mental health is not the same as diagnosing conditions.
ethicsAndBoundaries.title: Education vs Diagnosis
keyPoints: Apps and articles provide general knowledge.
Diagnosis requires training, context, and professional standards.

ethicsAndBoundaries.title: Limits of Self-Assessment
keyPoints: Personal insight is influenced by bias.
whyItMatters: Explains why clinicians gather broad context.

ethicsAndBoundaries.summary: Certain situations benefit from professional support.
ethicsAndBoundaries.title: When to Seek Professional Help
keyPoints: Persistent distress that interferes with daily life.
Significant changes in behavior or mood.
whyItMatters: Professionals are trained to assess risk responsibly.

ethicsAndBoundaries.summary: Mental health work follows strict ethical standards.
ethicsAndBoundaries.title: Ethical Responsibilities in Mental Health
keyPoints: Boundaries protect both clients and clinicians.
whyItMatters: Prevents harm and misuse of information.

stressAndCognition.summary: Stress activates biological systems designed to protect the body.
stressAndCognition.title: The Stress Response
keyIdeas: Energy is redirected toward immediate needs.

stressAndCognition.summary: Anxiety heightens sensitivity to potential danger.
stressAndCognition.title: Anxiety and Threat Perception
keyIdeas: The brain favors detecting threats over missing them.
Ambiguous situations may feel more dangerous.

stressAndCognition.summary: Stress changes how information is processed and remembered.
stressAndCognition.title: Stress Effects on Attention and Memory
whyItMatters: Clarifies why recall may feel unreliable.
keyIdeas: Details may be missed or distorted.

stressAndCognition.summary: Stress influences judgment and choice patterns.
stressAndCognition.title: Decision-Making Under Pressure
whyItMatters: Normalizes changes in thinking under pressure.
keyIdeas: Fast decisions are favored over careful analysis.

stressAndCognition.summary: Short-term and long-term stress affect cognition differently.
stressAndCognition.title: Acute vs Chronic Stress
whyItMatters: Explains why ongoing stress feels different.
Clarifies why rest and context matter.
keyIdeas: Acute stress is temporary and adaptive.
Chronic stress alters baseline cognitive function.

learningMemoryAttention.summary: Improved performance does not always mean learning has occurred.
learningMemoryAttention.title: Learning vs Performance
whyItMatters: Explains why cramming feels effective but fades.
Clarifies why struggle can support learning.
keyIdeas: Performance can improve temporarily without lasting understanding.

learningMemoryAttention.summary: Memories are rebuilt each time they are recalled.
learningMemoryAttention.title: Memory Is Reconstructive
whyItMatters: Clarifies why recollections differ between people.
keyIdeas: Memory is influenced by context and emotion.

learningMemoryAttention.summary: Forgetting is a functional part of memory systems.
learningMemoryAttention.title: Why Forgetting Exists
keyIdeas: Not all information is retained equally.

learningMemoryAttention.summary: The brain has limits on how much information it can process at once.
learningMemoryAttention.title: Cognitive Load

emotionRegulation.summary: Emotions provide information about internal states and external situations.
emotionRegulation.title: What Emotions Do

emotionRegulation.summary: Managing emotion differs from ignoring or eliminating it.
emotionRegulation.title: Regulation vs Suppression
whyItMatters: Clarifies common misunderstandings about emotional control.
Explains why suppression can be exhausting.
keyIdeas: Regulation involves modulating intensity or expression.
Suppression blocks expression without addressing experience.
Different strategies have different cognitive costs.

emotionRegulation.summary: Some emotional processes occur without conscious effort.
emotionRegulation.title: Automatic and Deliberate Regulation
whyItMatters: Explains why regulation feels harder under pressure.

emotionRegulation.summary: No single emotional response is always appropriate.
emotionRegulation.title: Why Context Matters
keyIdeas: Flexibility is central to healthy regulation.

emotionRegulation.summary: Emotions and thinking continuously influence each other.
emotionRegulation.title: Emotion and Cognition
whyItMatters: Integrates emotion with earlier cognition sections.

neuroscienceBasics.summary: The brain functions as interconnected systems rather than isolated parts.
neuroscienceBasics.title: The Brain as a Network
keyIdeas: Multiple regions contribute to most behaviors.
Damage or change affects systems, not single abilities.

neuroscienceBasics.summary: Brain cells communicate through electrical and chemical signals.
neuroscienceBasics.title: Neurons and Communication
whyItMatters: Explains learning at a biological level.
keyIdeas: Timing and patterns matter more than single signals.

neuroscienceBasics.summary: Different regions contribute differently to cognition and emotion.
neuroscienceBasics.title: Functional Brain Regions
keyIdeas: Some regions support attention and planning.

neuroscienceBasics.title: Neuroplasticity
keyIdeas: Connections strengthen or weaken over time.

neuroscienceBasics.summary: Brain science explains patterns, not certainties.
neuroscienceBasics.title: Limits of Neuroscience
keyIdeas: Context matters as much as biology.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Bias influences decisions even when people believe they are objective.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Attention limits how much information can be processed at once.
psychologyGlossary.definition: The selective focus on certain information while ignoring others.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Memory is reconstructive and influenced by context and emotion.
psychologyGlossary.definition: The process of encoding, storing, and retrieving information.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Plasticity explains learning and adaptation across the lifespan.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Clinical reasoning reduces error and premature conclusions.

psychologyGlossary.whyItMatters: Boundaries ensure safety, trust, and responsible practice.
psychologyGlossary.definition: Professional limits that protect individuals from harm or misuse.

All material is educational and non-diagnostic.
disclaimer: SolveMind does not provide medical, psychological, or legal advice.
This app does not diagnose, treat, or replace licensed professionals.
Always seek qualified professionals for medical or mental health concerns.
about.mission: SolveMind is an educational psychology app designed to help users understand how the mind works, how decisions are made, and how cognitive and emotional processes influence behavior. It is built for learning, reflection, and informed thinking — not diagnosis or treatment.

ai.summary: Short, focused prompts to strengthen decision quality and emotional regulation.
ai.title: AI Coach: Daily Reflection

b: Describe a decision you made today in 2–3 sentences.
What assumption did you treat as a fact?
What is one disconfirming piece of evidence you could look for?
Choose a reversible next step.
Clearer thinking under pressure, fewer default shortcuts, better outcomes.

ai.summary: A quick scan to identify common biases shaping the decision.
ai.title: AI Coach: Bias Check

b: Confirmation: Am I only noticing supporting evidence?
Availability: Am I over-weighting the vivid or recent?
Anchoring: Am I stuck on the first number or label?
Loss aversion: Am I over-fearing downside vs upside?
Overconfidence: Am I skipping uncertainty checks?
